question.problem:
Solve the following congruence:

$$
4x+3≡34\,(\text{mod}\,13),
$$

expressing your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $13.$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,13)$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce our congruence to a congruence of the form $ax≡b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+3 & ≡34\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 4x+3-3 & ≡34-3\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 4x & ≡31\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 4x & ≡2\cdot 13+5\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 4x & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=4$ and $n=13$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(4,13)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $4\,(\text{mod}\,13).$ To find the inverse of $4\,(\text{mod}\,13)$, we compute the exponents of $4\,(\text{mod}\,13)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,13):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{2} & ≡16≡1\cdot 13+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ {4}^{3} & ≡3\cdot 4≡12 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ {4}^{4} & ≡12\cdot 4≡48≡3\cdot 13+9≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ {4}^{5} & ≡9\cdot 4≡36≡2\cdot 13+10≡10 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ {4}^{6} & ≡10\cdot 4≡40≡3\cdot 13+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $10\cdot 4≡1\,(\text{mod}\,13),$ which means that $10$ is the multiplicative inverse of $4$ (modulo $13$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $10,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & ≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 10\cdot 4x & ≡10\cdot 5 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ (10\cdot 4)x & ≡50 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡11+3\cdot 13 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ x & ≡11 &  & (\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡11\,(\text{mod}\,13).$
